rationale: The flags experiment executed in a clean copy (0bd684d77ff947f7bb85883d5dbb3dc2, completed, exit 0) with all four of its comparisons complete and satisfied: under PreVote and CheckQuorum with the logical clock running, the re-added voter's invocation did not return inside the window and its payload was not committed, while the never-removed member's invocation returned and committed on all three nodes. This update records the configuration-robustness observation as durable knowledge and revises the parent interpretation to cite the new receipt, so the account no longer depends on default flags or on a clock that never advances.

knowledge.statement: The held-proposal effect persists under the recommended production configuration with a running clock. With Config.PreVote and Config.CheckQuorum enabled and ten rounds of ticks delivered with delivery between rounds, the leader remained node 1 in StateLeader at term 1 and the re-added node was a voter (index 38 of the receipt); its invocation had not returned after 900 ms inside a 1200 ms context (index 40) and its payload was committed nowhere (index 41), while the never-removed member's invocation returned with no error (index 43) and its payload was committed on all three nodes (index 44).
knowledge.conditions: Async Node API, three nodes (1,2,3) in one process with PreVote and CheckQuorum true, ElectionTick 10 and HeartbeatTick 1; node 3 removed by a committed simple ConfChange and re-added by a committed simple ConfChange with leader 1 unchanged; ticks delivered in ten rounds with delivery between rounds before the invocation; reliable delivery.

interpretations.joint_history: The witness series comes from the seven-receipt lineage of this investigation (43a04622beef40588679c6cf1c40d6ad, a9f71d7a07454d058d818148f7479e8f, 87b38a551d554c2391427dda00c4e6e4, 905d729b2a284c93bbbedd3c3a307ca8, 6e187216178a49d4ae02bd8c2afaeaf9, bd84c33f4fe647bc9470b0b48f324bca, e7cdea5042e54182b277e185ae576ea8) on the same fixed scenario, and receipt 0bd684d77ff947f7bb85883d5dbb3dc2 is its successor under PreVote and CheckQuorum with the clock running, so it shares the harness, node set, removal and re-addition procedure and differs only in configuration flags, the clock advance and event names. Receipt 99416a609e5242adbf53c527cc526cba comes from the child investigation's control experiment in the same harness: it contains the lineage's witness events for its own run (indices 7, 8, 9) plus the contrast case in which the member stays an outgoing voter (indices 37, 39, 40). All three receipts therefore describe the same witnesses and scenarios, and each cited index is either a witness-path observation or the boundary/flag variant of it.
interpretations.rationale: Eight retained executions of the witness scenario agree, the running clock and the recommended flags were both executed, and the necessary premise is witnessed by a control. In e7cdea5042e54182b277e185ae576ea8 (default flags, ten rounds of ticks) the witness invocation stayed pending at 2001 ms, the clock did not release it, and admission came only with a leader change (4637 ms) after which the payload committed. In 0bd684d77ff947f7bb85883d5dbb3dc2 (PreVote and CheckQuorum true, clock advanced before the invocation) the re-added voter was admitted (index 39), did not return within 900 ms (index 40) and its payload was committed nowhere (index 41), while the control member's invocation returned (index 43) and committed on all three nodes (index 44) with leader 1 still in StateLeader (index 38). In 99416a609e5242adbf53c527cc526cba the boundary case with the member kept as an outgoing voter returned and committed (indices 39, 40). Source account: the run loop's gate variable is assigned only at node.go:374 (leader observed), 377 (no leader) and 426 (local member removed) and used as the receive case at node.go:386; the removal guard fires exactly when applying a conf change deletes the local Progress entry, which LeaveJoint does for outgoing voters that are in neither the incoming half nor the learner set, while EnterJoint keeps the entry. The snapshot's own expectation (node_test.go:352-385) scopes intended blocking to a node that does not know the current leader, which is not the witnessed case. Controls now exclude cluster-wide stalls, a broken state machine, the clock and the flag settings as the cause, a single removal form, and the possibility that any configuration change disarms the gate.
counterevidence: node.go:407-411 acknowledges the gate as improvised (propc is reset when the leader changes ... This isn't very sound and likely has bugs); this explains the dependence on leader changes but is neither a calling restriction nor a protection, and no other re-arm path exists in the snapshot.

node_test.go:352-385 shows that not returning is intended for a node that does not know the current leader. That expectation does not cover the witnessed case, and the same test expects acceptance once a leader is known.
No request is lost: held invocations are admitted unmodified once the gate is re-armed, so the harm is an unbounded wait without an error signal rather than data loss or a protocol safety violation.
The control in the same harness and the control under PreVote and CheckQuorum both show the opposite outcome for a member that was never removed, so the effect is not a general proposal-path failure.
limitations: Comparison outcomes for the earliest receipt were unknown because that harness gave the three operations' result events the same names; its decisive events are complete and match the successor receipts, which have complete holds.

Scope is the async Node API path (node.run loop) in this snapshot; RawNode.Propose and RawNode.ProposeConfChange have no such gate. Delivery is reliable in the harness, so loss and partition behaviour is not characterized.

The clock schedules executed were ten rounds with delivery between rounds (default flags and PreVote plus CheckQuorum); other schedules and partitions where the member hears no leader traffic were not executed.

Removal forms executed: simple ConfChange removal and joint-implicit removal with automatic leave. The control covers an outgoing voter that is never left; other participant forms (incoming voter, learner) were not executed as controls.
The configuration-proposal case was executed once (add node 9) in one window; it establishes that the administrative entry point is affected, not a distribution over configuration-change kinds.
